original_test_intent: Verify that launching the intended BMC remote KVM creates or correlates to the expected management-session record and that closing the KVM causes that exact session to disappear or enter the documented closed/expired state within five minutes, without affecting other users' sessions.
original_method: Select the unique row; identify BMC/SUT/WebUI/KVM client and SessionService schema; record configured KVM/session timeout and existing redacted sessions; launch one KVM session with a dedicated test account and verify the displayed host identity; correlate the resulting KVM connection to an exact session URI/ID using creation time, account, client origin and vendor metadata; capture its open state; close the KVM normally and record time; poll only read-only session listings at bounded intervals through the full five-minute boundary and grace period; verify the mapped record alone is gone or terminal; close remaining test browser session per approved policy.
manual_activity: An operator supplies the authorized test account, confirms the correct KVM target and permitted close/final state; an agent may drive the approved browser session and perform redacted SessionService polling.
required_inputs: BMC/SUT firmware, WebUI and KVM client versions plus displayed target identity
Dedicated test account/role and SessionService schema/vendor fields mapping KVM connections to session resources
Configured timeout, definition of normal KVM close, polling interval, five-minute boundary/grace and expected absent/deleted/terminal representation
TLS/secret/session-redaction policy, concurrent-session baseline and recovery/cleanup procedure
safety_requirements: Verify displayed KVM host identity before any interaction and use a dedicated account
Do not send keyboard/mouse/power/virtual-media actions beyond what is needed to confirm connection
Never log credentials, cookies, tokens, Authorization headers or full sensitive session payloads
Map one test session uniquely before evaluating disappearance and never close other session resources
Stop on wrong target, ambiguous mapping, unexpected active control, API error, token leak or unrelated session change
agent_execution_scope: Capture redacted before/open/closed/poll SessionService views and KVM connection markers
Map the test connection by approved non-secret fields and calculate closure latency
Verify unrelated session identifiers remain stable and clean up only the test context
Do not expose tokens, terminate sessions through Redfish, interact with host workload, repeat login blindly or decide verdict
engineer_actions: Approve whether SessionService directly represents KVM and the exact correlation fields
Approve configured timeout, five-minute/grace oracle and closed-state representation
Approve test account/concurrency, safe KVM connection confirmation and final cleanup
Review stale/ambiguous session evidence and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Launching/closing KVM plus SessionService polling matches the source, but a raw session list does not prove which entry is KVM and hardcoded credentials/insecure TLS are prohibited.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use a dedicated browser/KVM context and TLS-validated protected Redfish session; capture redacted session metadata before launch, immediately after launch, at close, and bounded intervals through five minutes plus approved grace, tracking only the mapped test session.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: BMC Web KVM launch, Redfish session checks, normal close, five-minute timeout and 10/10-minute estimate remain.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a differential session inventory around one dedicated KVM launch, bind the added record by account/client/time/vendor metadata, then measure its removal/terminal transition after normal close while proving other records are unchanged.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds configured policy, unique session correlation, bounded polling, grace, sensitive-field hashing/redaction and unrelated-session invariants.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Comparing two anonymous session lists can mistake the persistent BMC Web login for KVM, or report success because another user's session ended while the test KVM leaked.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Some BMCs track HTML5 KVM in a vendor websocket/session store rather than standard Redfish SessionService, or keep the parent Web session after KVM closes; the authoritative mapping must be documented.

project_override_considerations: If standard SessionService does not expose KVM sessions, engineering must name the supported vendor session resource or approve a KVM-connection audit alternative; absence from an unrelated collection cannot pass the test. The five-minute wording should be treated as a maximum or exact/grace boundary only after policy approval.
expected_evidence: BMC/SUT/WebUI/KVM client and configured timeout identity
Dedicated account approval and redacted baseline concurrent-session inventory
KVM connected-target evidence plus added/mapped session URI or salted ID hash and correlation fields
Close timestamp and redacted bounded poll timeline through five minutes/grace
Mapped terminal/absence result and proof unrelated sessions stayed unchanged
No-secret/no-input audit, cleanup/recovery events and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source consistently uses Redfish session information to observe KVM launch/close and expects a five-minute cleanup. Whether that mapping exists is a vendor prerequisite rather than an internal contradiction.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The KVM lifecycle and timeout objective are clear. A supported mapping, authorized account and browser/Redfish access are supplyable inputs, so the case is not intrinsically blocked.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Functionality row 2242 Wistron-BMC Sanity-00024-V001: approve BMC/SUT/WebUI/KVM versions and whether/how a KVM connection maps to Redfish SessionService or a vendor session resource; define correlation fields, dedicated account/concurrency, configured timeout, normal-close behavior, polling interval, five-minute maximum/exact boundary and grace, expected absent/deleted/terminal state, sensitive-field redaction, cleanup and recovery.

review_improvement: Preserves the KVM open/close and five-minute Redfish observation while preventing an anonymous session-list difference or credential leak from being accepted as evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: A BMC Web login, KVM websocket and Redfish session token may be separate lifecycles. Closing the KVM should not necessarily terminate the parent Web session, and SessionService might expose one, both or neither depending on implementation. Therefore the test needs a differential inventory and vendor-approved correlation before timing removal. The five-minute wait is not itself risky, but remote-console authorization and session metadata are sensitive; read-only polling can be automated only inside those boundaries.
